notes: Evening Edition for Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026, published on request while the regular twice-daily schedule is paused (it resumes Thu, Nov 5). It covers news since Tuesday morning.

stories.headline: Democrats hold both chambers as the count goes on in Alaska, Mississippi and about 60 House races
stories.deck: A day after AP race calls gave Democrats control of the House and the Senate, two Senate races and roughly 60 House seats were still uncalled on Wednesday. The open races will set the size of the new majorities, not which party leads.
stories.summary: A day after AP race calls gave Democrats control of the House and the Senate, two Senate races and roughly 60 House seats were still uncalled on Wednesday. The open races will set the size of the new majorities, not which party leads. NPR, using AP race calls, reported that Democrats flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats (North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas, Iowa and Maine), returning them to full control of Congress for the first time since 2023. AP said that as of 4 p.m. ET Wednesday only a handful of Senate and governor races were uncalled and that 59 House races remained uncalled. El Cronista, citing AP tallies from Wednesday morning, put the Senate at 54 Democrats to 44 Republicans with Alaska and Mississippi still open. Slate reported on Wednesday evening that Democrats had officially won 237 House seats, with several Arizona, Florida, North Carolina and Colorado races among those still counting. California alone had 11 uncalled House seats, and its counties have until Dec. 3 to finish counting, El Cronista reported. Race-by-race results are in our Midterms 2026 special edition, listed under Past editions.
stories.why: Every extra seat changes how much room Democratic leaders have to pass bills, launch investigations and override, or fail to override, presidential vetoes when the new Congress meets in January.
stories.label: Reported
stories.note: Seat totals move as ballots are counted; figures here are as of the times the linked outlets published them on Wednesday. Donna Daily does not call any race.

stories.headline: Trump says the Iran war ‘probably’ cost Republicans, but he would do it again
stories.deck: Taking questions at a White House ballroom ceremony, President Trump agreed with Vice President JD Vance that the Iran war hurt Republicans by pushing up gas prices, and said he could work with Democrats “unless they want to be destructive.”
stories.summary: Taking questions at a White House ballroom ceremony, President Trump agreed with Vice President JD Vance that the Iran war hurt Republicans by pushing up gas prices, and said he could work with Democrats “unless they want to be destructive.” Speaking as the final steel beam went into the new ballroom on Wednesday, Trump said “if I were on the ballot, we would have won” and that Republicans “weren’t able to transfer the love” from his rallies to candidates, Fox News reported. Asked about Vance’s post blaming the war, Trump said “I think it’s largely true because it drove the gasoline up,” but that “if I had it to do again, I’d have to do it again.” He pointed to his veto power and said impeachment would “destroy” the Democratic Party.
stories.why: It is the president’s first public account of the defeat, and his veto threat previews the standoff a Democratic Congress now faces.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Quotes are as reported by Fox News from Trump’s remarks to reporters; Vance’s post is described as Fox News summarized it.

stories.deck: Democrat Scott Colom led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 65 votes out of nearly a million on Wednesday afternoon, Slate reported. In Alaska, Mary Peltola and Sen. Dan Sullivan were virtually tied with about three-quarters of the vote in.
stories.summary: Democrat Scott Colom led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 65 votes out of nearly a million on Wednesday afternoon, Slate reported. In Alaska, Mary Peltola and Sen. Dan Sullivan were virtually tied with about three-quarters of the vote in. Mississippi counts mail ballots postmarked by Election Day that arrive by Nov. 10, and state law provides no recount, El Cronista reported; a dispute could go to court or to the Senate itself. Alaska counts domestic mail ballots arriving by Nov. 13 and overseas ballots by Nov. 18. If no one passes 50%, the state runs its ranked-choice tabulation that day, with certification targeted for Nov. 25. Neither race can change which party controls the Senate.
stories.why: A Colom win would give Democrats a Senate seat in a state Trump carried by more than 20 points in 2024, per Slate; Alaska’s ranked-choice count could stretch the wait for weeks.

stories.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne is scheduled to table Budget 2026 on Thursday, Nov. 5. stories.deck: The Legislative Council passed a bill bringing in the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and updated Common Reporting Standard. Service providers start collecting data next year, with exchanges from 2028.
stories.summary: The Legislative Council passed a bill bringing in the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and updated Common Reporting Standard. Service providers start collecting data next year, with exchanges from 2028. The government welcomed the passage on Wednesday. Under the framework, crypto service providers will collect specified information so the Inland Revenue Department can exchange it with partner jurisdictions starting in 2028. The amended CRS takes effect in 2028, with financial account information exchanged under the new standard from 2029, on a reciprocal basis, the government said.

stories.headline: China’s central bank moves to slow the yuan’s rise with its first FX reserve increase in nearly five years

stories.summary: The People’s Bank of China said it will raise the share of foreign-currency deposits banks must hold with it from 4% to 6% from Nov. 15, Xinhua reported, a step meant to ease upward pressure on the yuan. It is the first increase in nearly five years. The yuan gained 4.2% against the dollar in the first nine months of the year, and the onshore rate strengthened for 14 straight trading days from Oct. 14, according to Xinhua. Raising the ratio drains dollar liquidity at banks, which tends to cool the currency. The South China Morning Post also reported the move as aimed at easing appreciation pressure.
stories.why: A fast-rising yuan squeezes Chinese exporters; the move signals Beijing wants the currency to stay broadly stable.

stories.headline: Como thrash Lens 9-1 to match the biggest win in modern Champions League history
stories.deck: Cesc Fàbregas’s Como, in their first Champions League campaign, won 9-1 away at Lens, with Anastasios Douvikas scoring a hat-trick, equalling the record eight-goal margin.
stories.summary: Cesc Fàbregas’s Como, in their first Champions League campaign, won 9-1 away at Lens, with Anastasios Douvikas scoring a hat-trick, equalling the record eight-goal margin. Only Liverpool (8-0 against Besiktas in 2007) and Real Madrid (8-0 against Malmö in 2015) had won by eight before, and Como are only the second team to score nine in a Champions League game, after Bayern Munich’s 9-2 win over Dinamo Zagreb, theScore reported. Elsewhere on Wednesday, Erling Haaland scored the winner in Manchester City’s 3-2 win at RB Leipzig, Real Madrid came from behind to win 3-2 at AEK Athens, and Liverpool lost 3-2 at Fenerbahçe, CBS Sports reported.
stories.why: A club in its first Champions League campaign has just matched one of the biggest results the competition has seen.
